blocks.title: Introduction
blocks.content: In coding theory, one of the classical problems is to determine $A(n, d)$, the maximum size of a binary $(n,d)$ code with length $n$ and minimum distance at least $d$. The (Hamming) distance distribution of a code is considered since the MacWilliams identities provide a linear relation between the distance distribution and its transform [@MS77]. With this linear relation, the maximum possible size of a code can be formulated as a linear programming problem. Semideﬁnite programming bounds for binary codes
from a split Terwilliger algebra
Pin-Chieh Tseng, Ching-Yi Lai, and Wei-Hsuan Yu
Abstract
We study the upper bounds for A(n, d), the maximum size of codewords with length n and Hamming distance at least d.
Schrijver studied the Terwilliger algebra of the Hamming scheme and proposed a semideﬁnite program to bound A(n, d). We
derive more sophisticated matrix inequalities based on a split Terwilliger algebra to improve Schrijver’s semideﬁnite programming

blocks.title: Terwilliger algebra and Schrijver's SDP
blocks.content: Let ${\cal P}$ be the power set of $\{1, \dots, n\}$. A binary code $C$ is a subset of ${\mathcal P}$. For $X,Y \in {\mathcal P}$, denote $$X\Delta Y= \{a\in\{1,\dots,n\}: a\in (X \setminus Y) \cup (Y \setminus X) \}.$$ Let $\lvert S \rvert$ denote the size of a set $S \in {\mathcal P}$. Hence the (Hamming) distance of $X$ and $Y \in {\mathcal P}$ is $\lvert X \Delta Y \rvert$. The distance distribution of the code $C$ is $$A_{j} = \frac{1}{\lvert C \rvert} \sum_{x \in C}\{ y \in C : \lvert x \Delta y \rvert = j\} \label{eq:dist_distriubtion}$$ for $j=0,\dots, n$. blocks.title: Semidefinite program
blocks.content: []{#sec:SDP label="sec:SDP"} In this section, we provide an SDP that gives an upper bound on the size of an $(n,d)$ code $C\subset {\mathcal P}$. We include the known linear constraints in the literature, which are critical in the SDP. We observe that an SDP with semidefinite constraints based on quadruple distances [@GMS12] does not improve the upper bounds of $A(18, 4)$ and $A(19, 4)$. In fact, the bounds obtained with only Schrijver's semidefinite constraints are even worse than the bounds with linear constraints [@Del73; @Bes80] in some cases. blocks.title: Semidefinite program for binary codes
The correctness of computer computational results
computational results
blocks.content:
We use the CVX toolbox [@GB14], [@GB08] in MATLAB with the MOSEK solver to run our SDP. Our main results are as follows. In our SDP, we have tested all possible values of splits $n_{1}$ and $n_{2}$. The computational results give us two improvements $A(18,4) \leq 6551$ and $A(19,4) \leq 13087$. However, using Gijswijt's method in the previous subsection, we are only able to ensure one of them is improved.

::: theorem
$A(18,4) \leq 6551$.
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Using $n_{1} = 2$, we obtain $A(18,4)\leq 6551.93$ with an error term less than $10^{-16}$. Thus $A(18,4)\leq 6551$. ◻

blocks.title: Generalization
blocks.content: []{#sec:gener label="sec:gener"} In this section, we consider an $m$-split distance distribution defined on a partition of $\{1, \dots, n\}$ with arbitrary $m$ subsets, say $T_{1}, \dots, T_{m}$, each of size $\lvert T_{p}\rvert = n_{p}$ for $p \in \{1, \dots, m\}$. Our method can be generalized in this case to introduce more semidefinite constraints. Proofs to these generalizations are similar to the $2$-split case and will be omitted. Finally, we discuss the underlying association scheme structure.\

Underlying structure
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:struct label="sec:struct"}

Herein we describe a special structure for an association scheme, which is inspired by the split method used in this paper.

::: definition
($m$-split property) Let $S = (X, \{R_{i}\}_{i=0}^{k})$ be an association scheme. blocks.title: Conclusion
blocks.content:
[]{#sec:conslus label="sec:conslus"} In conclusion, we have derived generalized Schrijver semidefinite constraints by considering the split of Terwilliger algebra. Our split semidefinite constraints are a natural generalization of Schrijver's constraints since they also implied the generalized Delsarte inequalities.

By implementing a $2$-split SDP, we have improved the upper bounds for $A(18, 4)$ and $A(19, 4)$. The MATLAB programs of the SDPs in this paper can be found at:

::: center
<https://github.com/PinChiehTseng/Split_SDP_solution>
:::
